title: AdaPipe: Optimizing Pipeline Parallelism with Adaptive Recomputation and Partitioning
problem: Pipeline parallelism for LLMs causes unbalanced and heavy memory consumption across devices. Recomputation techniques reduce memory usage but introduce significant computation overhead.
motivation: Large language models require distributed training systems where pipeline parallelism efficiency directly impacts scalability and training costs.
method: When training large language models across multiple devices (like GPUs or TPUs) in parallel, different pipeline stages run on different devices simultaneously. AdaPipe automatically decides for each intermediate value (temporary data computed during processing) whether to save it to memory or discard and recalculate it later, picking whichever is more efficient. It also automatically partitions the pipeline stages across devices to balance memory usage—preventing some devices from running out of memory while others have spare capacity—and reduces waiting time when devices need to synchronize.
key_novelty: AdaPipe jointly optimizes two normally separate decisions—which intermediate values to recompute (versus store) and how to partition pipeline stages across devices—to balance memory consumption against computation overhead.
contributions: Adaptive recomputation scheme for dynamic activation storage decisions
Adaptive pipeline partitioning algorithm for memory-balanced stage distribution
Integrated system design combining both techniques
Experimental demonstration of improved training throughput and memory efficiency

metrics.other: Peak memory reduction and memory utilization efficiency

limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract
primary_theme: Adaptive pipeline parallelism for large language model training
